Subject: HeliosBank RFP — Identity & Access follow-ups

Karthik —

Thanks for the initial RFP submission. The HeliosBank security and procurement team reviewed the identity section and have a few follow-ups so we can map to our controls matrix and procurement schedule: 

1) SCIM: Does Redwood support incremental user sync (PATCH) and group membership sync? Can you confirm support for custom user attributes and maximum payload sizes?

2) SAML / OIDC: Do you support both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SSO for SAML 2.0? For OIDC, do you support PKCE and dynamic client registration?

3) RBAC & admin controls: We need to confirm native roles, ability to create scoped custom roles, and delegated admin for separate business units. How are role assignments audited?

4) Evidence & artifacts: Procurement will need exportable audit logs, recent SOC evidence, and a short checklist for certificate rotation/downtime windows.

Can your team provide short written responses and any artifacts you can share (metadata, implementation guide, evidence bundle) by COB Wednesday 17 Feb?

Appreciate it — looping in procurement separately if needed.

Regards,
Sarah Jenkins
Senior Analyst, Identity Assurance
HeliosBank
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 11:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HeliosBank RFP — Identity & Access follow-ups

Sarah —

Thanks for the clear list. We'll do a short written response and attach the requested artifacts. High level commitments here so your team can proceed with procurement:

- SCIM: We support SCIM 2.0 (Users + Groups), PATCH operations for incremental updates, bulk replace, and custom attributes (we recommend namespacing with urn:helios:custom). Maximum practical payloads are subject to API throttling — we'll include recommended chunking guidelines in the guide.

- SAML/OIDC: We support SAML 2.0 (SP- & IdP-initiated), signed assertions, multiple NameID formats, and OIDC with PKCE. Dynamic client registration is supported for private deployments via our admin API; hosted customers can request client creation via Console for managed flows.

- RBAC/admin: Built-in roles include Owner, Admin, Operator, Viewer, and Security Admin. Custom roles are supported with granular permissions and scope (org, project, model). Delegated admin is available with role scoping per account and per-project. Audit trails for role changes are exported in JSON/CSV and are retained per the chosen retention policy.

I've attached our SAML metadata template so you can provision a test connection quickly. Marissa will send the SCIM guide and the implementation notes tomorrow with more detail and example mappings for group->role.

Would you like a 30-minute technical call Tuesday 16 Feb 09:00 PT to walk through mappings and cert exchange?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah —

Following up with the SCIM and RBAC detail Karthik promised. Key points below; excerpted from the attached SCIM guide. Attachment: redwood-scim-implementation-guide.pdf

SCIM specifics:
- Endpoints: /scim/v2/Users and /scim/v2/Groups.
- Supported operations: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE. PATCH follows RFC 7644 (JSON Patch) and supports replace/add/remove for attributes.
- Sync model: We support incremental sync via PATCH and timestamp-based queries (filter by meta.lastModified). For large directories we recommend pagination + delta tokens; examples included in the guide.
- Custom attributes: Supported. Use fully-qualified attribute names to avoid collisions; we recommend urn:helios:<attribute>. Maximum attribute count per user: 256, maximum attribute value length: 16KB.
- Error handling: 429 backpressure responses with Retry-After; bulk replace will return per-item error details.

RBAC & role mapping:
- Default roles: Owner (full), Admin (org-level manage), Operator (deploy/run), Viewer (read-only), SecurityAdmin (audit + policy).
- Custom roles: Create via Console or Admin API; permissions are additive and can be scoped to organization, project, or model.
- Group->role mapping: Map SAML group claim or SCIM group membership to Redwood roles. Example mapping: helios-admins -> Admin, helios-ops -> Operator. Mappings can be enforced or treated as suggestions depending on account config.
- Delegated admin: Support for sub-account admins (separate billing/controls) with activity separation.

Operational notes:
- Role-change audits are recorded with actor, timestamp, originating IP, and change delta. Exportable as CSV/JSON and accessible via Console or API.
- Certificate rotation: We support hot-swap of signing certs for SAML with overlap windows; minimal impact if performed during a scheduled maintenance window. Template included for rotation steps.

I'll join the tech call if you confirm the 16 Feb slot. If you need any custom claims or mappings pre-populated prior to the call, share a small sample CSV and we'll create a staging configuration.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-scim-implementation-guide.pdf

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 16:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HeliosBank RFP — Identity & Access follow-ups

Hi Sarah and team —

Thanks for the procurement checklist. Quick security/evidence summary and what we can provide immediately: 

1) Audit logs: Standard hosted retention is 13 months for full API/auth/audit trails; exports available as compressed JSON or CSV (per-range). Logs contain actor_id (internal id), actor_display_name, action, target_resource, timestamp, request_ip, and change_delta. PII: by default we do not log full secrets or raw credential values; usernames and email addresses are included where required for tracing. We can provide redacted exports on request.

2) Encryption & keys: Data at rest is encrypted with AES-256. For hosted customers we manage keys via a cloud KMS; for Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) with rotation policies and HSM-backed keys for on-prem deployments. Key rotation process documented in the evidence bundle.

3) Evidence artifacts: Attached is an evidence bundle that contains: SOC 2 Type II summary (redacted), pen-test executive summary, configuration screenshots for SSO & SCIM mapping, and a sample audit export. Attachment: redwood-iam-evidence-2027-02.zip

4) Other notes: We support signed and encrypted SAML assertions, strict clock tolerance settings, and validations for audience and recipient. OIDC flows support PKCE and token revocation endpoints.

If procurement needs a notarized SOC package or a detailed penetration test artifacts we can arrange an NDA and a secure upload to your vendor portal. Let us know the portal instructions and preferred file format (zip/tar).

Best regards,
Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-iam-evidence-2027-02.zip
